t: Count Number of Possible Root Nodes — Rerooting
o: Given an unrooted tree and Bob's parent-guesses, count roots for which at least k guesses are correct. Brute force tries every root and re-counts in O(n^2). The efficient tool is rerooting: compute the score for root 0 with one DFS, then derive each neighbor's score in O(1) — moving the root across edge (u,v) invalidates guess (u->v) and validates guess (v->u), changing the score by exactly -1/+1.
k: Score(root) changes predictably when the root moves along one edge: only the guessed orientation of that edge flips.
Store guesses in a hash set keyed by (u, v) for O(1) lookups during both DFS passes.

a.i: First DFS from node 0 counts correct guesses top-down. Second DFS pushes scores: when moving from u to child v, score(v) = score(u) - [guess (u,v) present] + [guess (v,u) present]. Every node's score is exact, so count those >= k.
s: Encode each guess as u*N+v in a hash set.
DFS1: return, for each subtree rooted at u (parent p), the count of guesses (a,b) with a on the path orientation parent->child; accumulate into score[0].
DFS2: propagate score[v] = score[u] - has(u,v) + has(v,u).
a.t: O(n + m) — two DFS passes over the tree plus hashing the guesses.
a.sp: O(n + m) — adjacency list, guess set, score array, recursion stack.

a.i: For each candidate root, orient the tree via DFS/BFS and count matching guesses. O(n·(n+m)) — educational baseline that TLEs at n = 1e5 but validates the rerooting logic on small inputs.
s: For each root r: BFS/DFS assigning parents.
a.t: O(n(n+m)) — a full traversal per candidate root.
a.sp: O(n + m) — adjacency, parent array, queue.

w: Rerooting is the intended technique and a staple interview pattern (also used for 'sum of distances' problems). Pitfalls: deep recursion in Python (raise the limit or go iterative), pair-encoding collisions (use u*(n+1)+v or a string key), and sign errors in the transfer formula. Follow-up: answer queries 'how many roots give exactly j correct guesses' by bucketing scores.
